root_idea.summary: The non-hamz root is organized around directed pursuit or deliberate aiming and, in another branch, sharpness; from directed, attentive discernment develop meanings of knowing, tactical observation, and related instruments.
root_idea.development: Classical analysis connects knowledge with discerning or finding something through attention, skill, or artifice. The sharpness branch yields terms for pointed grooming and hunting instruments, while hamz-bearing forms belong to a distinct push or repulsion root and are not treated as meanings of this Quranic root.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I is presented under its normalized perfect-tense dictionary citation form.
Quran-attested Form IV is presented under its normalized perfect-tense dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To know, be aware of, or have knowledge of something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with a direct object or with بِ. Classical descriptions can emphasize knowledge reached after doubt or through discernment and skill, but the Quranic occurrences express knowing or awareness without requiring that special nuance.

senses.definition: To make someone know something; to inform, acquaint, or disclose it to them.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic rhetorical construction ما أَدْرَاكَ, the verb asks what can or will make the addressee know and is followed by an explanatory statement. In ما يُدْرِيكَ, the corresponding question is presented without that subsequent explanation in the Quranic usages discussed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deceive, delude, beguile, circumvent, or outwit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage may involve concealing oneself while deceiving a person or an object of the chase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To scratch the head or to comb, loosen, or separate hair with a pointed grooming tool.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action is described with the instrument مِدْرًى or مِدْرَاة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To winnow ore dust in order to separate its gold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a dialectal variant; the lexical source also suggests that this report may be an error for ذَرَّى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat someone gently or with blandishment; to soothe, coax, wheedle, or cajole them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived noun also covers good nature and familiar, conciliatory intercourse. With عن or على, the construction can mean trying to turn or entice someone away from or toward a matter by blandishment or deceitful arts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deceive, beguile, circumvent, or outwit someone, or to strive to do so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct Form III usage from the gentling or conciliatory sense, though the two can occur in related dealings with another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To defend someone by speaking, pleading, or contending on their behalf.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَنْ in the cited defensive construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take for oneself or prepare a دَرِيَّة, a hunting decoy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical Form IV usage distinct from the Quranic causative meaning ‘to make know.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an army, for one part to press upon another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported in a specialized expression and described as though formed in place of يَتَدَرَّأُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To direct one's course toward a place in an inroad or incursion against an enemy, with intent to fight or plunder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The report is phrased in the assimilated expression اِدَّرَوْ مَكَانًا and may also be used of an apparent rather than actual incursion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Knowledge or awareness, as a verbal noun of دَرَى.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is reported with variant vocalizations and is also used in the expression مِنْ غَيْرِ دُرْيَةٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An act or deed in the expression مِنْ غَيْرِ دُرْيَةٍ, ‘without any act or deed.’
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic use reported for the same nominal form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beast used as a hunting decoy, behind which the hunter conceals himself before shooting at game.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal is variously described as a camel, she-camel, cow, or other beast; the lexical point is its use as concealment for the hunter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wild animal or game animal, especially one pursued in the hunt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a use of the noun for the hunted animal rather than for the decoy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing or ring used as a target for learning to pierce or thrust with a spear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is associated with training in spear work.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pointed instrument for scratching the head or arranging, separating, or combing hair; also a horn used for such a purpose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related forms مِدْرَاة and مَدْرِيَة are cross-referenced as names for the same type of implement. A horn of a wild bull or gazelle can be used in this role.

cautions: The evidence distinguishes the non-hamz دري family from hamz-bearing دفع-related forms; those neighboring forms are not assigned as meanings of this root.
The Form II ore-winnowing report is explicitly qualified as dialectal and possibly an error for ذَرَّى.
Classical evidence discusses, and restricts, using الدَّارِي as a divine epithet; this is a usage and naming issue, not an additional Quranic sense.
